text: When setting project goals, it is essential to use the SMART framework. This means your goals should be Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound. For example, instead of saying "improve the website," a SMART goal would be "increase page load speed by 20% within three months." Once your goals are defined, break them into smaller milestones. These are checkpoints that help you track progress and stay motivated. Each milestone should lead to a clear deliverable, such as a completed report or a working prototype. Finally, ensure stakeholder alignment. Regularly communicate with everyone involved to confirm that your objectives match their expectations. This prevents misunderstandings and keeps the entire team moving in the same direction.
